intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (PVRL1; 600644) on chromosome 11q23.3. Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7).

checks.claim: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome (CLPED1) is caused by homozygous mutation in the NECTIN1 gene (PVRL1).
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome on Margarita Island, CLPED1 (ref. 1).
checks.explanation: The abstract states that homozygosity for a PVRL1 (NECTIN1) mutation causes CLPED1.

checks.claim: The NECTIN1 gene is located on chromosome 11q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygosity for a nonsense mutation of PVRL1, W185X, results in an autosomal recessive CL/P syndrome
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper names, so it counts as supported under the rules. The abstract itself does not mention 11q23.3.

checks.claim: Heterozygosity for a NECTIN1 mutation has been associated with sporadic nonsyndromic cleft lip with or without cleft palate (OFC7).
checks.evidence_quote: Here we demonstrate highly significant association between heterozygosity for this mutation and sporadic, non-syndromic CL/P in northern Venezuela.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly states the association between heterozygosity and sporadic non-syndromic CL/P.

paragraphs.text: Cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder. Suzuki et al. (1998) described its features as unusual facies, dental anomalies, hypotrichosis, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, onychodysplasia, syndactyly, and cleft lip/cleft palate. Some patients have also had intellectual disability (Zlotogora et al., 1987; Rodini and Richieri-Costa, 1990; Yoshida et al., 2015).

paragraphs.text: Bustos et al. (1991) described 27 individuals from 7 families, related to each other with high probability, from a relatively isolated and inbred population on Margarita Island in northeastern Venezuela (Nueva Esparta State). The affected individuals had features of ectodermal dysplasia along with other anomalies, with variable expressivity, and females were affected as severely as males. The authors stated that the clinical picture shared by all patients could not be classified among the known ectodermal dysplasias.

paragraphs.text: Yoshida et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old Japanese boy, the first child of a consanguineous marriage, with cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia syndrome. He had hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia with sparse, brittle, fine, dry hair and hypodontia, a unique facial appearance with cleft lip/palate, cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers, and mild mental retardation. Scanning electron microscopy of the hair showed pili torti and pili trianguli et canaliculi. The authors stated that this was the first report of an Asian individual with the syndrome.
